name: s06-individuality
title: Evolutionary individuality
question: Does generational group selection on a heritable adhesion trait produce a response that requires clonal group structure (evolutionary individuality)? (Q5)
hypothesis: Group-level selection on adhesion yields a heritable multi-generation response in clonal groups that vanishes without selection (drift null) and is weakened when groups are mixed (non-clonal).
claim: Clonal group-level selection on a heritable adhesion set-point produces a multi-generation evolutionary response: seed-mean mean-adhesion rises +0.22 on held-out seeds 4-6 (+0.32 on training seeds 1-3) over 6 generations, exceeding the selection-off drift null and reaching the highest group cohesion (toughness ~0.93). Clonality is required for full trait transmission (heritability 1.0 clonal vs 0.5 mixed) and the mixed-founder response is attenuated (+0.14 held-out). QUALIFIED: the clean selection-vs-drift margin is on training seeds (+0.33 over a ~0 null); on held-out seeds the drift null itself drifts up ~+0.10 (boundary reflection of the lower-bounded [0,0.6] init), narrowing the held-out margin to +0.12. Heritability is structural (fixed by the clonal/mixed encoding), not emergent; the emergent result is the response. within_group is ~0 in every arm, so non-clonal founding collapses heritability by trait dilution, not active within-group conflict.

behavior_tests.name: between-group-heritable-fitness-stable
behavior_tests.description: Out-of-sample (seeds 4-6): seed-mean adhesion response (mean_adhesion last - first emitted generation) of clonal+selection exceeds clonal drift null and is > 0. Secondary: heritability(clonal) > heritability(mixed) and mixed-sel response < clonal-sel response. Seeds 1-3 are characterization only.

controls.name: selection-off-drift-null
controls.rationale: Same founding and reseeding, selection off: any adhesion change is drift/reseeding. The response must vanish here.

controls.name: mixed-adversarial-arm
controls.rationale: Non-clonal groups dilute the heritable trait; tests whether clonality matters. See limitations: this works by trait dilution, not active within-group conflict.

alternative_hypotheses.name: reseeding-artifact
alternative_hypotheses.statement: The adhesion change is an artifact of the reseeding procedure, not selection.

alternative_hypotheses.name: clonality-irrelevant
alternative_hypotheses.statement: Clonal structure is irrelevant to the response.
alternative_hypotheses.excluded_by: clonal vs mixed comparison of response and heritability

alternative_hypotheses.name: seed-luck
alternative_hypotheses.statement: The response is specific to the seeds used to characterize it.

limitations: Ruling R-S06-DILUTION: in the mixed arm the within_group Price term is ~0 because adhesion carries NO intrinsic within-group growth advantage under uniform growth; cheaters do not out-compete founders inside a patch. The mixed control therefore collapses heritability by TRAIT DILUTION (heritability toward ~0.5) and weakened among-group selection, NOT by active within-group conflict.
Short horizon: 6 generations, one CPM backend (viva-cpm), 2D, 3 seeds per split.
Only provided mechanisms are modelled; no adhesion-linked fitness cost, so the study does not test conflict-mediated loss of individuality.

Drift-null boundary bias: founder adhesion is initialised in [0,0.6] and clipped to [0,1], so the selection-off random walk reflects upward (held-out drift +0.10 vs training -0.01). The clean selection-vs-drift margin is on training seeds (+0.33); the held-out margin (+0.12) is the selection effect net of this bias, since both arms share the clip.
Heritability (1.0 clonal / 0.5 mixed) is structural — fixed by the clonal/mixed encoding — not an independent emergent measurement; the emergent quantity is the multi-generation response.
falsifiability: Clonal selection response not exceeding the drift null on held-out seeds 4-6 overturns the claim.
A drift-arm response comparable to the selection arm indicates a reseeding artifact.
Heritability or response equal in clonal and mixed arms would show clonality is irrelevant.
discovery_implications: If supported, clonal group structure plus selection suffices for a heritable group-level response; whether non-clonal groups can sustain it depends on conflict mechanics not modelled here.

followup_study_proposals.title: Adhesion-linked fitness cost (active within-group conflict)
followup_study_proposals.rationale: Add a growth cost to adhesion so cheaters out-compete founders within a patch; then the within_group Price term becomes nonzero and the mixed arm tests conflict suppression, not only trait dilution (ruling R-S06-DILUTION).

followup_study_proposals.title: Centred / symmetric adhesion init to remove the drift boundary bias
followup_study_proposals.rationale: Initialise founder adhesion around 0.5 (or widen generations) so the selection-off random walk is unbiased, giving a cleaner held-out selection-vs-drift margin.

config.title: Clonal group selection evolves adhesion; the drift null and mixed arm are weaker

findings.statement: Seed-mean mean-adhesion response over 6 generations (held-out seeds 4-6 | training seeds 1-3): clonal+selection +0.224 | +0.324; clonal drift null +0.101 | -0.008; mixed+selection +0.138 | +0.096; mixed drift +0.101 | -0.008. Group toughness: clonal-sel ~0.93, clonal-drift ~0.82. All 24 runs completed; numbers from analysis/grade_individuality.py.
findings.inferential_scope: 6 generations, 6 potts seeds per arm, one CPM backend (viva-cpm), 2D.

findings.statement: Mechanism: group fitness = largest-cluster toughness (reuses S04 fracture); the Price partition splits the group-adhesion change into among-group (Cov(w,z)) and within-group (E[w*dz]) terms. among_group is positive for selection arms and ~0 for drift; within_group is ~0 in EVERY arm because adhesion carries no intrinsic within-group growth advantage under uniform growth. Heritability (parent-offspring regression of group adhesion) is 1.0 clonal / 0.5 mixed, fixed by the clonal/mixed encoding (structural, not emergent).
findings.inferential_scope: Engineered generational loop; Price terms computed, not validated against data.

findings.statement: Clonal group-level selection evolves a heritable adhesion increase (individuality emerges) that the drift null does not; clonality is required (mixed response attenuated, heritability halved). QUALIFIED — the clean selection-over-drift margin is on training seeds (+0.33); on held-out seeds the drift null drifts up ~+0.10 (boundary reflection of the [0,0.6] init), leaving a modest +0.12 margin. The mixed (non-clonal) control collapses heritability by trait DILUTION, not active within-group conflict (R-S06-DILUTION): with adhesion as the only trait, cheaters have no within-group fitness advantage.
findings.inferential_scope: Seeds 4-6 held out; 6-generation horizon; 2D; one CPM backend; a-priori-fixed parameters.
